question.text: Roshni Trust (education for disabled) holds a Section 12AB certificate that expires in 8 months from the date of NSE SSE application. The CFO insists that Section 12AB status exists and is 'sufficient'. As SIA, what is the CORRECT position under Table 3.1 of the SSE framework?

answer.text: The 12AB certificate must be valid for AT LEAST the next 12 months from the date of application.
Any valid 12AB certificate on the application date is sufficient; residual validity is immaterial.
The 12AB certificate must be valid for at least 24 months.
12AB is optional if the NPO has FCRA registration.

explanation.text: The Logic: Table 3.1 explicitly requires the Registration certificate under Section 12A/12AA/12AB/10(23C)/10(46) to be valid for at least the next 12 months from the date of application. An 8-month residual validity fails this test, and the SIA must flag this as a gating deficiency — the NPO should first apply for renewal (usually at least 6 months before expiry under the IT Act) and then return to SSE. The Trap: Option A ignores residual-validity requirement. Option C doubles the correct threshold (24 vs 12). Option D wrongly equates FCRA with 12AB — they are separate regimes (one for foreign contribution, one for income-tax exemption). Cross-Exam Context: X-A/X-B (IA) cover 12A/12AB from the donor-deductibility angle. XXIV/IFSCA-01 (AML) overlap on FCRA sanction-list screening. XIX-A (AIF) covers trust structures but not 12AB residual validity. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Build a 'regulatory residual-validity matrix' as part of every SSE engagement: date, expiry, months-to-expiry, renewal-in-progress Y/N. Any line < 12 months is a hard stop. Also verify the 12AB order number on the income-tax portal (search 'Exemption Online') — some NPOs submit stale certificates.
